title: Tiered Consumption Smoothing & Conditional Accrual Framework for Renewal Negotiations
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Large customers experience bursty usage that causes unpredictable true-ups at renewal. Sales and Customer Success report long negotiations and churn risk when customers face sudden overage charges. We need a standardized framework to smooth renewal upsells via conditional accruals (on-book credits) that preserve revenue while reducing friction and time-to-close for multi-year deals.

Proposal summary: Introduce a Tiered Consumption Smoothing & Conditional Accrual Framework (TCSCAF). Key elements: (1) a ledger of "accrued credits" tied to committed renewal bands that vest over the contract term based on usage trajectories, (2) a set of standardized uplift/forgiveness rules for multi-year commitments, (3) a procedural checklist for Security Questionnaire (SQ) alignment on contract language about credits/true-ups, and (4) an experiment to validate commercial uplift and negotiation time reductions.

Primary goals: reduce renewal friction, shorten negotiation cycles by 20% (target), reduce churn due to surprise true-ups, and preserve or grow ARR when customers expand.

Scope: enterprise renewals where committed spend >= $200k ARR or where historical monthly volatility > 40%. Pilot limited to 12 accounts across EMEA and North America in H1 2025.
acceptance_criteria:
- Framework documented and approved by Revenue Operations and Legal.
- Finance models show <=5% short-term ARR downside at pilot scale with expected NPV-neutrality over 24 months.
- Pilot onboarding runbook created and CS/AE training completed.
- Two pilot renewals completed with observed negotiation time delta logged.
- Instrumentation in billing to track accrued credit ledger and true-up reconciliation is available in 'Renewals Dashboard' (dataportal link).
implementation_notes:
Phase 1 (design & legal): draft credit ledger mechanics, sample contract clauses, and SQ language. Legal to provide a 'plain english' clause for SOWs and renewal addenda.
Phase 2 (engineering & finance): minimal billing engine changes to tag and track accrued credits as non-expiring ledger entries (for pilot). Build a reconciliation job for end-of-term true-up.
Phase 3 (pilot & measurement): select pilot cohorts, run 90-day pilots, collect metrics.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Simpler approach: one-time upfront credit vs accrual ledger. Upfront credits are easy but blunt; accrual ledger ties incentives to usage and preserves revenue if customers never reach uplift bands.
- Risk of accounting complexity; Finance recommends pilot ledger entries be off-balance until final true-up to simplify reporting.
- Complexity vs PS overhead: more granular vesting rules require CS enablement and more negotiation templates. We will start with 2-tier vesting rules to limit PS burden.
rollout_plan:
1) Legal/RevOps sign-off (2 weeks); 2) Billing prototype & reconciliation job (4 weeks); 3) CS/AE playbook & training (1 week); 4) Pilot activation for 12 accounts (90 days); 5) Evaluate and decide: scale, modify, or sunset (2 weeks).

Canary controls: only enable for accounts tagged with 'pilot-smoothing' in CRM. Initial financial guardrails: cap total accrued credits to 10% of yearly committed value per account.
metrics:
- Negotiation time (days) pre/post pilot for participating accounts.
- Renewal conversion rate for pilot vs matched control.
- Average true-up delta at renewal and percent of accrued credits consumed.
- ARR delta and net revenue retention (NRR) impact.
- Support/PS hours spent on renewals.
- Dashboard endpoints: /dashboards/renewals/consumption-smoothing, billing reconciliations job logs.
